description.narrative:
Oxfam is a global movement of people creating lasting solutions to the social injustice of poverty and inequality. Launched in 2013, the Women’s Economic Empowerment and Care (WE-Care) program is Oxfam’s flagship initiative to increase women’s and girls’ time andchoice to participate in social, economic, and political life by transforming how unpaid care and domestic work (UCDW) is valued, shared, and invested in. For this proposal, Oxfam America will be the lead applicant and contract holder, assuming the overall responsibility for the successful delivery of the grant; coordinating reporting to the Foundation, and ensuring compliance with all Hewlett Foundation terms and conditions. Oxfam America has served on the WE-Care Steering Committee since 2014, and is highly familiar with the Hewlett Foundation, its staff, policies, requirements, and ways of working, having directly managed more than $20 million in grants from the Foundation in recent years.
In Africa, the WE-Care Programme is overseen by the Oxfam in Africa (OiA) Gender Justice Lead, who heads OiA's Gender Justice Pillar. Within this pillar, WE-Care falls under the Women Economic Justice Care thematic area. Oxfam in Africa is a regional platform of Oxfam International, the global secretariat of the Oxfam confederation, based in Nairobi.
WE-Care aims to increase the recognition of UCDW in public policy; reduce heavy and time-consuming UCDW through investments in essential public services and infrastructure; redistribute the responsibility for UCDW more equally between men and women and between households and the state; and ensure that women with care responsibilities are represented in the planning and implementation of budgets and policies that affect their lives. The program works towards a just and inclusive society by recognizing, reducing, redistributing, representing, and rewarding unpaid care and domestic work (UCDW), which will increase their ability to live their lives to the fullest and enjoy better social, economic, political, and cultural rights. It envisions a world where women and girls have more choice at every stage of their lives and that the work they do is valued. The program has previously been implemented in the Philippines, Zimbabwe, Ethiopia, Uganda, and Kenya. Continuing Phase V, in September 2024, WE-Care phase 5.2 will focus on African women andgirls gaining greater autonomy over their lives . The new phase will also focus on strengthening institutional capacities of WE-Care partners. The program will be implemented in Zimbabwe, Ethiopia, Uganda, and Kenya with strong linkages to regional and global influencing spaces.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
